item.title: Correction · Crane Cove Park: The Crane Cove Park page now says the crane cabs were cut from the…

item.title: Correction · Crane Cove Park: Several Crane Cove Park details were tightened: the $17.8 million…
item.description: Several Crane Cove Park details were tightened: the $17.8 million contract was one of five, the $36.7 million total is a capital-plan figure that includes work finished after opening, and the acreage and the YMCA location now follow the Port's own wording. A $565,000 contract-increase request is shown as an agenda item, not a cost. Source: Port Commission agenda, 2022-04-12 (https://sanfrancisco.granicus.com/AgendaViewer.php?view_id=92&clip_id=40995); Port Commission staff report Calendar Item 11C, 2016-09-08 (https://sfport.com/sites/default/files/2016-9-13%20Staff%20Report%20Crane%20Cove.pdf); Port Resolution 18-61 memo, 2018-11-08 (https://sfport.com/sites/default/files/Planning/Resolution%2018-61%20Contract%202812%20Park%20Improvements%20Award%20to%20Gordon%20N%20Ball.pdf); Port staff report Item 12B, 2018-09-07 (https://sfport.com/sites/default/files/Planning/Item%2012B%20Crane%20Cove%20Park%20Informational.pdf); Port staff report, 2015-10-13 (https://sfport.com/sites/default/files/2015-10-15%20Staff%20Report%20Crane%20Cove.pdf); Port 10-Year Capital Plan FY2024-33 draft, 2023-05 (https://www.sfport.com/files/2023-05/050923-9a.1_capital_plan_draft_2024-2033.pdf); Port news release, 2025-12-12 (https://www.sfport.com/about/news/port-san-francisco-opens-child-play-areas-and-dog-run-crane-cove-park).

item.title: Correction · Crane Cove Park: The 2018 entry's early-2020 opening forecast now notes that Crane…
item.description: The 2018 entry's early-2020 opening forecast now notes that Crane Cove Park actually opened on September 30, 2020. Source: Pier & Point editorial review.

item.title: Correction · Crane Cove Park: The record now describes a stabilized historic gantry crane (not two…
item.description: The record now describes a stabilized historic gantry crane (not two restored cranes), a boating center and cafe as future development opportunities for Building 49 rather than built scope, and the ~$4 million fundraising as for the crane tops and play structures; the entrance claim and 'preliminary and final design' were removed. The 2017 photo caption no longer calls Nov 2018 a construction start; the Tbo47 panorama is dated 2026-06-28 from its Exif date on Wikimedia Commons; and the schematic-design exhibit is dated by its Oct. 8, 2015 memo and Oct. 13 meeting. The map notes no longer say the park has no Assessor lot, that Figure 6.4.2 covers only 28 acres, or that the 69-acre plan has four components with ~5- and ~28-acre parts. Two earlier change entries about Port Commission agenda items now say they were requests, not approvals, and the 2011 award is described as a request listed by the Port. Source: Port of San Francisco, Resolution 18-61, 2018-11-13 (https://sfport.com/sites/default/files/Planning/Resolution%2018-61%20Contract%202812%20Park%20Improvements%20Award%20to%20Gordon%20N%20Ball.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 12B staff report, 2018-09-07 (https://sfport.com/sites/default/files/Planning/Item%2012B%20Crane%20Cove%20Park%20Informational.pdf); Wikimedia Commons, File:Crane_Cove_Park.jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Crane_Cove_Park.jpg); Port of San Francisco, Crane Cove Park staff report, 2015-10-13 (https://sfport.com/sites/default/files/2015-10-15%20Staff%20Report%20Crane%20Cove.pdf); Port Commission agendas, 2020-12-08 (https://sanfrancisco.granicus.com/AgendaViewer.php?view_id=92&clip_id=37252) and 2022-04-12 (https://sanfrancisco.granicus.com/AgendaViewer.php?view_id=92&clip_id=40995).

item.title: Milestone · Crane Cove Park: Port Commission hearing on staff's request to… (Sep 13, 2016)
item.description: Port Commission hearing on staff's request to authorize award of Contract 2740 (Crane Cove Park Surcharge and Site Preparation) to Shimmick Construction Company for $4,110,000 plus a 10% contingency, a total not to exceed $4,521,000 (staff memo dated Sep 8, 2016; the Port's project page lists the request under Sep 13, 2016 and the authorization to award as 2016; the vote itself is not shown in the sources read); construction through this contract started in November 2016 and was complete by the time of the November 2018 award memo, and the project page dates site preparation complete to 2017 (Sep 13, 2016). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2016-09-08; Port of San Francisco; Port of San Francisco, 2018-11-13; Port of San Francisco.

item.title: Milestone · Crane Cove Park: Port Commission approves the Crane Cove Park project… (Oct 13, 2015)
item.description: Port Commission approves the Crane Cove Park project and the fourth and final sale of 2008 Clean and Safe Neighborhood Parks GO Bonds ($8,695,000); estimated total project cost $31,475,904; Phase I to deliver about five acres of an eventual ten-acre park (Oct 13, 2015). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2015-10-13.

item.title: Milestone · Crane Cove Park: Port Commission calendar lists a request to award the… (Jun 14, 2011)
item.description: Port Commission calendar lists a request to award the master planning and preliminary design contract (June 14, 2011; AECOM, selected competitively); initial estimate about $30 million for the whole park, with $10 million secured from the 2008 Parks GO Bond (the cited hearing index could not be read when this was checked, so the award itself is confirmed only by the 2018 report's statement that the Commission approved a contract with AECOM) (Jun 14, 2011). Source: Port of San Francisco; Port of San Francisco, 2018-09-07.
